title: Navigating One Health impacts of rugged terrain: challenges and opportunities
content:
Abstract
Terrain ruggedness increasingly shapes health outcomes but remains understudied, especially from a One Health perspective, which emphasizes the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health. Rugged terrain affects One Health through direct pathways such as movement modification, access regulation, microclimate formation, and hazard buffering. These factors influence human health by limiting access to resources and affect animal health by increasing disease vulnerability in isolated populations, whereas physical isolation may also reduce zoonotic transmission risks. Environmentally, rugged terrain helps conserve biodiversity and habitats but can intensify erosion and runoff. Indirectly, rugged terrain influences One Health by increasing vulnerability to natural disasters and altering ecosystem services. These multidimensional effects position terrain ruggedness as both a protective factor and a vulnerability driver within One Health systems. Advancing integrated research on terrain-driven mechanisms is crucial for promoting human and animal health, conserving biodiversity, and supporting sustainable land management in complex landscapes.
